title: dcp config get reply (schema MAJOR 1)
description: What Aurora expects from `dcp config get --json --dir <root>`, offered when `dcp version --json` lists the capability `config` with schema_major 1. Unknown fields are ignored; MINOR versions only add optional fields and new values of a setting's `type`. Exit code 0 with this reply on standard output; any other exit code is a failure and standard error explains it. Every setting the protocol knows is listed, set or not, with its effective value; no setting carries a secret value.

root.description: The repository root the reply is about (absolute path)

revision.description: Opaque token that changes whenever the configuration file changes (for example a hash of its bytes, or `none` when there is no file); `config set --revision` refuses a different one

source.description: The configuration file read (path relative to root, normally .dev-cycle.json), or null when only defaults apply

settings.description: In the order to show them; groups appear in the order of their first setting

findings.description: Configuration problems found (unknown keys, invalid values, legacy keys), never blocking for the reader

value.description: A value of an editable setting: boolean, integer, text, list of text, or null when there is none

key.description: Dotted path in the configuration file, for example devops.branching or test_commands. A read-only setting may be display-only: shown for information and not stored in the file (its set is then always false)

group.description: Display group, for example devops, architecture, backlog

description.description: One line on what the setting does

type.description: The kind of value, which decides the control: enum, boolean, text, integer or list (of text). Readers treat any other type as read-only and show its value as it is, so a new type can come in a MINOR version. Structured settings that fit none of the five (for example a list of objects such as drift_rules) are listed with read_only true

set.description: true when the key is present in the configuration file; false when value is a default or a detected value. A key written in the file is a decision the user took, even when it equals the default; a key not set was never decided

value.description: The effective value: the file's value when set, else the default or the detected one. A value of the setting's type for an editable setting; any JSON value for a read-only one

default.description: The value that applies when the key is not set, null when the protocol falls back to detection or to nothing; same rule as value

allowed.description: The accepted values of an enum, or of each item of a list; null when any value is accepted

nullable.description: Whether null (no value at all) is an accepted value. Any set key of an editable setting can be removed with null in dcp.config-set, whatever this says

read_only.description: true for settings that are shown but not changed through dcp config set: mandatory gates and principles, structured settings, and keys owned by another command (for example speckit.enabled and speckit.version, written by dcp speckit init and upgrade)

read_only_reason.description: Why it cannot be changed, when read_only is true, naming the command or file to use instead when there is one
